description: SQL-backed client-matter validation and ethical walls middleware with Ollama admin dashboard
readme_excerpt:
# Matter Wall AI Admin

SQL-backed client-matter validation and ethical walls middleware with an administrator dashboard and optional Ollama AI assistant.

## What It Does

- Validates whether a user can open or work on a client/matter.
- Checks ethical wall access before downstream systems expose matter data.
- Provides admin CRUD screens over the SQL tables.
- Uses Ollama locally to help administrators summarize wall risks and draft remediation steps.

## Architecture

- `FastAPI` backend
- `SQLite` default SQL database
- Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript admin dashboard served by the API
- Optional Ollama integration at `http://localhost:11434`

## Quick Start

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -e .[dev]
matter-wall seed
matter-wall serve
```

Open:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

## Middleware APIs

Client-matter validation:

```http
POST /api/middleware/client-matter/validate
```

Ethical wall check:

```http
POST /api/middleware/ethical-walls/check
```

See [docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md) for SQL schema, API examples, dashboard workflows, and implementation notes.

description: Matter-segregated retrieval over legal documents, entirely on local infrastructure. Ethical walls enforced at retrieval, verified by test — nothing leaves the network.
readme_excerpt:
# Private Legal RAG

The retrieval system from `02-construction-claim-rag`, deployed entirely on local
infrastructure. No document, query, or embedding leaves the network.

## The problem

The barrier to AI adoption inside law firms is rarely capability. It is that
client documents are privileged, outside counsel guidelines frequently restrict
where client data may be processed, and clients increasingly audit their firms'
security posture directly. A tool that requires sending documents to a third
party API is a non-starter for a large share of a firm's matters regardless of
how well it performs.

## Who this is for

Firm IT and security teams evaluating whether AI over client documents can be
done inside their own perimeter.

## What this demonstrates

- Local model serving and local embedding, no external inference calls
- Local vector store, no hosted index
- Query and retrieval audit logging sufficient for an internal review
- **Matter-level access segregation** — retrieval is filtered by the requesting
  user's matter access before ranking, so a user cannot retrieve from a matter
  they are walled off from

That last item is the part most retrieval systems get wrong. Ethical walls are
not a preference, and a system that enforces them only in its answer layer while
retrieving across everything has already failed.

## Deployment and data residency

See `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` — architecture, data flow, and what an auditor would
want to see.

## Access control

See `docs/ACCESS_CONTROL.md` — the segregation model, its threat model, and its
known gaps.

## Running it

```sh
python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Ingest the sample corpus (three synthetic matters; embeds locally)
python -m private_rag ingest data/sample

# Query as a user — every query is identity-bound and audited
python -m private_rag query "crane inspection findings" --user alice
python -m private_rag query "escrow release condition" --user alice   # walled: nothing responsive
python -m private_rag query "escrow release condition" --user bob

# Deletion that means it
python -m private_rag forget ATLAS-LTR-001
python -m private_rag close-matter atlas-escrow

python -m private_rag audit
pytest   # includes the segregation suite; runs fully offline

# Grounded answers from a local model (requires Ollama + `ollama pull qwen3:8b`)
python -m private_rag ask "What is the dispute over the escrow release?" --user bob
python -m private_rag ask "What is the dispute over the escrow release?" --user alice  # walled: honest refusal

# Local web UI on http://127.0.0.1:8765 — identity picker, the documents
# that identity can see, and chat over the store. Same enforcement path
# as the CLI; the picker is the demo stand-in for SSO (see ACCESS_CONTROL).
python -m private_rag s

description: Measured results of a private, local-only legal RAG system — hybrid retrieval with reranking, cited answers, refusal discipline, ethical walls. Benchmarks honest, failures included.
readme_excerpt:
# Sovereign Legal RAG — Results **Private document intelligence for legal teams, running entirely on hardware the firm controls.** This repository publishes what the system achieves — measured retrieval quality, real sample behavior, and honest limitations. The engine itself (code, prompts, pipeline, and tuning) is private and deployed for clients. > Built by [MushiSenpai](https://theinvalid.me) as the application layer of the > [Sovereign AI Deployment](https://theinvalid.me/services) offer. Everything > below was measured on **real public legal data** (expert-annotated commercial > contracts), so the numbers are on the kind of documents a firm actually has — > not toy data. --- ## What it does - **Hybrid retrieval with reranking** — semantic search *and* exact-term search (defined terms, party names, `Section 12.4(b)`) fused into one ranked list, then reranked for precision. Lawyers search both ways; the system catches both. - **Pinpoint citations** — every answer cites `[document, page/section]`. - **Refusal discipline** — answers only from retrieved text; when the documents don't contain the answer it says exactly that, instead of inventing. - **Ethical walls** — a user retrieves only documents in matters they're cleared for; walled documents can't surface in an answer *or* a citation. - **Tamper-evident audit** — every query, role, and surfaced document is logged to an append-only, hash-chained audit log. - **Local-only, zero egress** — no cloud API, no per-token bills. The only network call is to the firm's *own* LLM endpoint. Unplug the network; it still answers.

--- ## Measured retrieval quality 150 clause-localization questions over real, expert-annotated commercial contracts (CUAD v1). A **hit** = a retrieved chunk contains the annotated answer span. description: Adversarial proof harness for ethical walls in legal AI retrieval — generates leak probes from a firm's wall topology and emits a signed attestation
readme_excerpt:
# Ethical wall attestation

Adversarial proof harness for information barriers in legal AI retrieval.
Every direct access-control test passed. All seven walls were breached anyway.

> An independent prototype exploring a problem in legal AI deployment. Not
> affiliated with or endorsed by any company. The firm, matters, lawyers and
> documents are synthetic. Not legal advice.

## The gap

An ethical wall is a court-recognised information barrier screening a lawyer from
matters where a prior client relationship creates a conflict. Index a firm's
documents for AI retrieval and those barriers must survive into the index.

The industry agrees. Harvey's own writing on agents and ethical walls notes that
agents access data autonomously, carry context across time and operate beyond
human monitoring, and concludes *"You can't have autonomous agents and manual
ethical wall compliance."* Intapp, the system of record for walls at most firms,
prescribes access controls, screen decisions and audit logs.

Nobody publishes a **procedure for proving the walls actually held**. That proof
is re-derived by hand at every deployment.

## Try it

```bash
npm install
npm run walls probes                                 # probes generated from the topology
npm run walls ingest                                 # derive topology from source exports
npm run walls attest --engine naive-matter-filter    # 0/7 walls hold
npm run walls attest --engine matter-scoped          # 7/7 walls hold
npm run walls attest --from-sources --engine matter-scoped \
  --conflicts fixtures/intapp-conflicts-degraded.json \
  --dms fixtures/imanage-security-degraded.json      # INDETERMINATE
npm test
```

Exits non-zero on breach, so it runs as a CI gate.

## The result

| Naive | Leak path | Hardened |
| ---: | --- | ---: |
| **0** | Direct retrieval — the only path a conventional access test covers | 0 |
| **32** | Context carryover — a permitted first turn leaves documents in the window | 0 |
| **23** | Citation leakage — sources are requested instead of content | 0 |
| **40** | Fact aggregation — permitted documents reconstitute a restricted fact | 0 |
| **12** | Metadata disclosure — a helpful refusal names what it refused | 0 |

The naive engine filters retrieval by the lawyer's staffed matters. That is the
standard approach, and it passes every direct access test. It breached all seven
walls through the four paths nobody tests.

Both engines face an **identical** probe set — asserted by a test, so the harness
cannot be tuned per engine.

        Check the contracts tracker.

description: Law firm matter workspace prototype: Microsoft Entra ID sign-in, role-based access and ethical walls on Supabase RLS, automatic SharePoint matter folders via Microsoft Graph.
readme_excerpt:
# Matter Workspace prototype

A small, real implementation of the four things that decide whether a custom
matter-management system survives contact with a law firm:

1. **Microsoft Entra ID sign-in** (OpenID Connect, single tenant, delegated Graph token with silent refresh).
2. **Roles enforced in the database**: attorney, paralegal, supervisor. Every query runs under Postgres row-level security keyed to the signed-in email. The UI cannot over-fetch.
3. **Ethical walls**: a walled person cannot see the matter, its members, its documents link, or the fact that a wall exists. Supervisor visibility is overridden too.
4. **SharePoint provisioning**: opening a matter creates `Matters/<no> - <client>/` plus nine standard sub-folders through Microsoft Graph, using the signed-in user's own permissions, and stores the link on the record.

Everything a user does is written to an audit table under the acting identity.

## Stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App | Next.js (App Router, server actions, TypeScript) | One deployable, server-side secrets, no client-side tokens |
| Identity | Auth.js with the Microsoft Entra ID provider | Standard OIDC, tenant MFA and conditional access stay with IT |
| Data | Supabase Postgres with row-level security | Policies live next to the data; a UI bug cannot leak a row |
| Documents | Microsoft Graph, root site document library | Delegated calls, so SharePoint permissions still apply |
| Hosting | Vercel | Zero-ops for a prototype; the app is stateless and portable to Azure |

## How the security model works

The app never uses the Supabase service key. On every request it signs a
five-minute HS256 JWT containing `email` and `app_role` for the acting user, and
Supabase evaluates policies against those claims:

```sql
-- excerpt from supabase/schema.sql
create function can_see_matter(m uuid) returns boolean ... as $$
  select not is_walled(m)
    and ( jwt_role() = 'supervisor'
       or exists (select 1 from matter_members where matter_id = m and email = jwt_email())
       or exists (select 1 from matters where id = m and responsible_attorney = jwt_email()) );
$$;
create policy matters_read on matters for select using (can_see_matter(id));
```

Walls are checked first, so a supervisor who is walled off a matter loses it too.
Walled users cannot read `matter_walls`, so they cannot discover that a wall exists.

### Demo control

One Microsoft account is flagged `is_demo_admin`. That account gets a "run every
query as" switch in the header. It only changes the identity in the signed JWT;
the database does the rest. This is how one login can demonstrate all three
roles and the wall. It is a demo affordance and would be removed for production.
